java.say: An enclosure starts in the closed state. It keeps its current state in a field.
To open the enclosure, it asks its current state to handle it, and keeps the state that comes back.
In the closed state, open() opens the gate and returns a new OpenState. From now on, the enclosure is open.
In the open state, open() changes nothing and returns this: the state stays the same.
close() works the same way. Enclosure has no if or switch on its state; each state class knows what to do.
